stories.summary: Replace the private _handlers peek with an explicit EventBus.delivers()
stories.description: ADR 0010 rule 5. persistence._notify_user reads the bus's private _handlers map to decide whether to write a notification itself; with a broker the consumer lives in another process, so every notification would be written twice.

TARGET IMPLEMENTER: cloud open-source (Claude-class sizing, every mechanically checkable requirement graded below). Provider/model are NOT pinned: dispatch resolves them from the live model registry's `roles.dispatch` entry.

WHY: `pipeline/persistence.py` `_notify_user` does `if not getattr(bus, "_handlers", {}).get("notification"): _write_directly()`. That is correct for `InProcessEventBus` only. A broker-backed bus has no local handlers in the publishing process, so the publisher would write the notification directly AND the remote consumer would write it again.

WHAT TO BUILD (behavior-preserving for every existing bus):
1. pipeline/events.py: a concrete (non-abstract) `EventBus.delivers(self, event_type: str) -> bool` whose default returns whether `self._handlers` (when the subclass has one) has a non-empty list for that type; `InProcessEventBus` and `JsonlEventBus` inherit it unchanged. Document the contract from ADR 0010 rule 5 in the docstring: "will a subscriber, local or durable remote, receive this type?".
2. pipeline/persistence.py: replace the `getattr(bus, "_handlers", {})` read with `bus.delivers("notification")`, guarded so a bus object without the method (a test double) falls back to the old private read. Keep the surrounding comment's reasoning, updated to name `delivers`.
3. `grep -rn "_handlers" pipeline app --include=*.py` must then return only pipeline/events.py.

TESTS (new tests/unit/test_event_bus_delivers.py): in-process bus with and without a notification subscriber; JsonlEventBus likewise; `_notify_user` writes directly exactly once when nothing delivers and does not when a subscriber does (count lines in the plan's notifications log); a stub bus whose `delivers` returns True suppresses the direct write even with an empty `_handlers` (the broker case).

stories.summary: Publish events to NATS JetStream behind PIPELINE_EVENT_BUS=nats
stories.description: The publishing half of the NATS adapter: a synchronous facade over nats-py that waits for the broker's ack, with fail-closed configuration.

WHAT TO BUILD (new module pipeline/events_nats.py; at most 3 public names: `NatsEventBus`, `EventPublishError`, `nats_settings_from_env`):
1. Config, all validated at bus construction (fail closed, ADR 0004; messages name the variable, never a credential): `PIPELINE_NATS_URL` (required); `PIPELINE_NATS_CREDS_FILE` (optional; must exist with mode 0600 or construction raises); a non-loopback URL must use `tls://` (or `nats://` with `PIPELINE_NATS_TLS_CA_FILE` set) - plain-text to a remote host raises; `PIPELINE_NATS_STREAM` (default `PIPELINE`); `PIPELINE_EVENT_PUBLISH_TIMEOUT_S` (positive number, default 5); `PIPELINE_NATS_MANAGE_STREAM=1` creates the stream (subjects `pipeline.>`, max age 7 days, file storage) if missing, otherwise a missing stream raises at construction.
2. Synchronous facade: one private asyncio loop on a daemon thread, created lazily on first use and re-created if `os.getpid()` changed (never reuse a loop across fork - ADR 0010 consequences). `publish(event)` sends to `pipeline.<type>.<plan>` (re-validate the plan with the same rules `JsonlEventBus._validate_plan` uses) with header `Nats-Msg-Id` = `event_id` or `idempotency_key` when present, waits for the JetStream PubAck up to the timeout, else raises `EventPublishError` (message names the subject's event type, not the payload). `subscribe(type, handler)` records the handler for BR-04's consumer runner; `delivers(type)` is True for every type with a recorded handler OR listed in `PIPELINE_NATS_DURABLE_TYPES` (default `notification,agent_done`), because the daemon consumes those durably.
3. pipeline/event_wiring.py: `PIPELINE_EVENT_BUS=nats` (the selector EV-02 added) builds `NatsEventBus` and subscribes the same three handlers `build_bus()` subscribes today.
4. requirements.txt: `nats-py` pinned to an exact version.
5. Call sites: confirm `_notify_user`, dispatch's `agent_dispatched` publish and worktree_patch's publishes already tolerate a raising publish (read each); report any that do not in the PR description rather than changing them here.
6. CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml test job): download a pinned `nats-server` release, verify its published sha256, start it with `-js` on 127.0.0.1, and set `PIPELINE_REQUIRE_NATS_TESTS=1`.

TESTS: tests/integration/test_nats_bus.py starts `nats-server -js` on a random port when the binary is on PATH, else SKIPS - except when `PIPELINE_REQUIRE_NATS_TESTS=1`, where a missing binary FAILS (no silent skip in CI). Add NATS to BR-02's base-tier parametrize list and its durable-tier list for the publish-side cases (dedup, publish timeout). Unit tests for every config refusal (missing URL, plaintext remote URL, world-readable creds file, bad timeout, missing stream without manage flag).

stories.summary: Consume durable events in the scheduler daemon with redelivery and dead-lettering
stories.description: The consuming half: durable pull consumers in exactly one process (ADR 0010 rule 6), acknowledging only after the handler returns.

WHAT TO BUILD (new module pipeline/events_nats_consumer.py; pipeline/scheduler_daemon.py is ~988 lines - add at most 3 lines there):
1. `start_consumers(bus)`: for each type in `PIPELINE_NATS_DURABLE_TYPES`, a durable pull consumer named `pipeline-<type>` with `max_deliver = PIPELINE_EVENT_MAX_DELIVER` (default 5) and exponential backoff. Fetch in batches on the bus's loop thread; for each message run the recorded handlers in order; ack after all return; on an exception, nak with the backoff delay; on the final delivery, publish the raw message to `pipeline.deadletter.<type>.<plan>`, write an `event_dead_lettered` record DIRECTLY to the plan sidecar (call the persistence direct-write path, never `_notify_user`, which would publish through the failing bus), log WARNING with the event type and handler name only, and ack.
2. Only the scheduler daemon calls `start_consumers`, and only when the bus is a `NatsEventBus`; MCP servers and the dashboard never consume. Stop consumers cleanly on daemon shutdown.
3. Redelivered `agent_done` must stay harmless: `wake_handler` already returns `check_precondition`'s refusal for a stale event, and `advance_pipeline` returns `skipped: locked`; add a test proving a duplicate `agent_done` causes no second dispatch.

TESTS (integration, same nats-server fixture and skip/require rule as BR-03): durable tier of BR-02 now runs for NATS - redelivery after a raising handler, dead-letter after max deliveries with exactly one sidecar record, consumer restart resumes without loss, duplicate agent_done is a no-op; unit: a non-NATS bus never starts consumers; shutdown stops the fetch loop.
